study_design: Retrospective model development on public dataset
patient_characteristics: Kaggle Stroke Prediction Dataset, adults over 18 years; stroke prevalence 5.53%
intervention_technology: Stacking (Naive Bayes, Random Forest, J48, RepTree; meta-learner Logistic Regression), WEKA
comparator: Single classifiers (NB, RF, 3-NN, J48, RepTree, LR, SGD, MLP)
validation_strategy: SMOTE applied to the whole dataset, then 10-fold cross-validation on the balanced dataset of 6148 instances (sample-level, no held-out test set)
limitations: Oversampling before cross-validation lets synthetic neighbours of test-fold cases enter training (data leakage), inflating AUC/recall; single public dataset without external validation
ground_truth_quote: "For our experiments, 10-cross validation was applied to assess the models' efficiency in the balanced dataset of 6148 instances" (Section 4.1 Experiments Setup); "Stacking classification outperforms the other methods, with an AUC of 98.9%, F-measure, precision and recall of 97.4% and an accuracy of 98%" (Abstract; Section 5 Conclusions, para 3); "The number of participants was 3254" (Section 3.1 Dataset Description, para 1)
source_location: Publisher PDF (SSoT): p.1 Abstract; p.3 Sec 3.1; p.8 Sec 4.1; p.10 Sec 5

study_design: Retrospective model development on public dataset
patient_characteristics: Kaggle Stroke Prediction Dataset (Soriano, 2021), 11 features; 58.6% female
intervention_technology: Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, SVM, KNN after class rebalancing (resampling preferred over SMOTE)
validation_strategy: 80/20 train-test split plus stratified 5-fold cross-validation applied post-resampling
limitations: All models showed poor recall: LR detected 0 of 50 test stroke cases despite 95.11% accuracy; accuracy-driven evaluation on imbalanced data; sample-level split
ground_truth_quote: "Logistic Regression yielded the highest mean accuracy (0.9511) and a strong ROC-AUC of 0.8362" (Results, Models performance para 1); Table 2: LR TN 972, FP 0, FN 50, TP 0; Gradient boosting FN 49, TP 1; "all models demonstrated poor recall, reflecting challenges in identifying rare stroke cases" (Abstract); "only 249 of 5,110 observations" and "stroke cases accounted for only 4.9% of the total" (Results, PDF p.11)
source_location: Publisher PDF (SSoT): p.1 Abstract; p.9 Data preprocessing; p.11 Models performance; p.13 Table 2

study_design: Retrospective model development on public dataset
patient_characteristics: Kaggle Cerebral Stroke Prediction-Imbalanced Dataset, 10 risk factors
intervention_technology: RF, XGBoost, KNN, SVM, MLP with random under-sampling; SHAP interpretation
validation_strategy: Nested stratified 10-fold cross-validation; random under-sampling in each run; hyperparameters tuned on training folds only
limitations: LR matched or beat complex models on AUC; under-sampling discards majority data; no external validation; accuracy around 70% after rebalancing
ground_truth_quote: "The dataset contains a total of 43,400 subjects and 10 risk factors" (Data Description); "a nested stratified 10-fold cross-validation process was adopted" (Section 2.6 para 1); Table 3: LR AUC 83.30, sensitivity 78.12; MLP sensitivity 81.40, FN rate 18.60
source_location: Full text PMC9600473: Data Description; Sec 2.6 para 1; Sec 4 para 2; Table 3

study_design: Retrospective model development on public dataset
intervention_technology: RDET stacking and soft-voting ensembles (RF, DT, ExtraTrees) with SMOTE / ADASYN
comparator: Single ML classifiers (RF, ETC, AdaBoost, SGD, KNN, DT)
validation_strategy: Oversampled (SMOTE/ADASYN) data divided 80/20 into training and testing sets; K-fold evaluation (Table 6)
limitations: Oversampling is applied before the train/test split, so synthetic copies of test cases are in training (explicit data leakage); 100% accuracy and recall with SMOTE are artefacts
ground_truth_quote: "the total number of participants is 3,254" (Abstract); "The stacking method achieved a remarkable accuracy of 100% as well as exceptional F1-score, precision, and recall score" (Results); "As with using SMOTE for balancing the dataset, RF, ETC achieved a 0.98 AUC score" (ROC curves para 3); "Next, the oversampled data is divided into training and testing sets" and "A total of 80% of the data is employed for training the classifiers and 20% for testing" (Methods); Table 6: SMOTE stacking accuracy 100, recall 100; ADASYN stacking accuracy 96.4, recall 97; "4,861 individuals classified as normal (healthy) and 249 individuals with a stroke" (Dataset)
source_location: Full text PMC10703010: Abstract; ensemble evaluation para 2; ROC curves para 3; Table 6

study_design: Retrospective EHR cohort (Shenzhen Health Information Big Data Platform)
patient_characteristics: Hypertensive patients; 9421 stroke onsets in 3-year follow-up; 19,953 samples after balanced sampling
intervention_technology: XGBoost, Random Forest, SVM with multitemporal trend features
comparator: Logistic Regression and traditional risk scales
validation_strategy: Case-control balancing by gender/age, random 7:3 train-test split; 5-fold CV on training set
limitations: Artificially balanced evaluation set does not reflect real prevalence; retrospective single-region data
ground_truth_quote: "a total of 57,671 patients were screened from 250,788 registered patients with hypertension, of whom 9421 had stroke onset" (Abstract); Table 3: XGBoost AUC 0.9220, recall 0.8512; LR AUC 0.8544, recall 0.7141; "the final 19,953 samples were randomly divided into a training set and test set according to a ratio of 7:3" (Abstract)
source_location: Publisher PDF (SSoT): p.1 Abstract; p.7 Table 3; p.9 Principal Findings

intervention_technology: RF, SVM, XGBoost, LightGBM, k-prototype clustering, SHAP
validation_strategy: Down-sampling of non-stroke group, then random 80/20 train-test split
limitations: Modest discrimination (AUC around 0.70) once a real cohort is used; down-sampling before the split changes test prevalence
ground_truth_quote: "comprising 7389 participants and 53 variables" (Abstract); Table 3: RF AUC 0.71 ± 0.06, recall 0.70 ± 0.05; LR AUC 0.68 ± 0.06
source_location: Full text PMC11276746: Abstract; Sec 2.7 para 5; Sec 3 para 4; Table 3

study_design: Cohort derivation (Framingham Offspring) and external validation (Boston Medical Center)
patient_characteristics: Stroke-free adults over 40; 18,793 visits; validation cohort 17,527 multi-ethnic patients
intervention_technology: Optimal Classification Trees (non-linear stroke risk score)
validation_strategy: External validation in a separate multi-ethnic cohort
limitations: Several visits per participant in derivation data; interpretable tree but drop from 87.43% to 75.29% on external data
ground_truth_quote: "inclusion of 4,385 unique participants, which translated in 18,793 distinct visits" (Derivation cohort para 2); "validation 75.29% (CI 0.74-0.76) vs 65.93% (CI 0.64-0.67)" (Abstract); "validated in a prospective multiethnic cohort of 17,527 patients" (Validation cohort para 1)
source_location: Full text PMC7241753: Abstract; Derivation cohort para 1-2; Validation cohort para 1

study_design: Retrospective pooled cohort (Framingham Offspring, ARIC, MESA, REGARDS)
patient_characteristics: Black and White adults aged 45 or older, free of stroke/TIA; 29% Black
intervention_technology: Two newly developed machine learning algorithms
comparator: Framingham stroke model, REGARDS self-report model, pooled cohort equations
validation_strategy: 10-year risk; discrimination and calibration by race, sex and age subgroups
limitations: ML did not significantly improve discrimination; all models discriminated worse in Black individuals (abstract-level extraction)
ground_truth_quote: "The combined study sample included 62 482 participants" (Abstract); "existing stroke-specific risk prediction models and novel machine learning techniques did not significantly improve discriminative accuracy for new-onset stroke compared with the pooled cohort equations" (Abstract, Conclusions); "All algorithms exhibited worse discrimination in Black individuals than in White individuals" (Abstract)
source_location: Abstract only (PMC10408266 full text not retrievable via Europe PMC API)

patient_characteristics: 58 ML stroke-prediction studies from five databases
validation_strategy: Descriptive synthesis (no meta-analysis due to heterogeneity)
limitations: Searched Google Scholar/ResearchGate and open access only; reports accuracy rather than recall; African populations represented in fewer than 4 studies; high-performing studies often relied on Kaggle data of unclear provenance
ground_truth_quote: "Fifty-eight studies were included" (Abstract); "ensemble methods consistently achieved highest accuracies for stroke occurrence prediction (range: 90.4-97.8 %)" (Abstract); "African populations, despite highest stroke mortality rates globally, were represented in fewer than 4 studies" (Abstract); "most high-performing studies relied on small, region-specific datasets or open-access data of unclear provenance (particularly Kaggle datasets)" (Discussion, PDF p.8)
source_location: Publisher PDF (SSoT): p.1 Abstract; p.8 Discussion

study_design: Systematic review of ML on routine hospital data (PubMed, 2013-2024)
patient_characteristics: 49 studies: 38 general population, 11 atrial fibrillation populations
intervention_technology: Various ML models on routine hospital data
limitations: Reviewed studies often had limited data quality, suspected overfitting, and lacked calibration, external validation and explainability
ground_truth_quote: "we identify 49 original research (38 in the general population and 11 in AF specific populations) articles" (Abstract); "with AUCs ranging from 0.64 to 0.99" (Abstract); "there was a high suspicion of overfitting and models often lacked calibration, external validation and explainability analysis" (Abstract)

study_design: Literature review of US ML stroke studies (PubMed)
limitations: Training datasets did not match where stroke burden is highest, threatening generalizability
ground_truth_quote: "Of the 27 studies included, 7 (25.9%) used patient data from California" (Abstract); "a strong disconnect exists between the datasets and patient cohorts used in training machine learning algorithms ... and the stroke distribution" (Abstract, Conclusions)
